content.title: Platform Overview
content.content: SnapLogic's architecture separates the control plane (cloud-hosted) from the data plane ({{deployment_type}}). This section details the platform components relevant to {{customer_name}}'s on-premises deployment requirements.

subsections.title: High-Level Platform Architecture
subsections.content:
SnapLogic's platform architecture is designed for hybrid and on-premises enterprise deployments where data sovereignty, security, and regulatory compliance are paramount. The architecture separates concerns between the control plane and data plane:

[IMAGE:assets/images/customer/airbus_vendor_profile/High_Level_Architecture.png:SnapLogic Deployment Architecture for Airbus Helicopters On-Premises Platform]

**Control Plane: SnapLogic Manager (Cloud-Hosted)**

The Manager is the cloud-hosted control plane responsible for:
- Pipeline definitions and metadata (no customer data)
- User authentication and RBAC configuration
- Scheduling and orchestration instructions
- Audit logs and usage analytics
- Designer UI and development environment

**Data Plane: Ground Plex (On-Premises)**

The Ground Plex is the on-premises execution engine responsible for:
- All pipeline execution and data processing
- All connector calls to SAP, databases, APIs, file systems
- All data transformation and business logic
- Credential storage (encrypted locally, never sent to cloud)
- Real-time monitoring and health metrics

**Key Architectural Principle for {{customer_name}}:**

No customer data ever transits the SnapLogic cloud. All data processing occurs within {{customer_name}}'s data center. The Ground Plex communicates with the Manager over a single outbound HTTPS connection (port 443) to receive pipeline definitions and send execution status. No inbound firewall rules required. No data egress.

[TABLE:accent-blue:Informatica to SnapLogic Terminology Mapping]
| Informatica Concept | SnapLogic Equivalent | Key Difference |
|---------------------|---------------------|----------------|
| Mapping / Workflow | Pipeline | Visual canvas, executable as-is — no code generation step |
| Transformation / Stage | Snap | 700+ pre-built, configured not coded |
| Integration Service / DTM | Ground Plex | Containerised on OpenShift, scales horizontally |
| Repository / Domain | Manager (cloud) | Metadata only — no data transits the Manager |
| Mapplet / Reusable Mapping | Child Pipeline | Modular, reusable, called inline |
| Folder / Repository Folder | Project / Org | RBAC-governed hierarchy: Org → Project Space → Project |
[/TABLE]

subsections.title: Ground Plex — On-Premises Data Plane
subsections.content:
The Ground Plex is SnapLogic's on-premises execution engine. It is the heart of the deployment for {{customer_name}} — the component that makes SnapLogic genuinely on-premises rather than cloud-first. Every pipeline execution, every data transformation, and every connector call happens inside the Ground Plex, inside {{customer_name}}'s private data center. The Ground Plex communicates with the SnapLogic Manager exclusively over a single outbound HTTPS connection (port 443). No inbound firewall rules. No data egress.

[IMAGE:assets/images/customer/airbus_vendor_profile/Screenshot 2026-04-27 at 21.19.05.png:Ground Plex Architecture and Deployment Model]

**Deployed as Docker containers on RedHat OpenShift**, managed via SnapLogic-certified Helm charts

**Each Ground Plex node runs multiple JCC (Java Cloud Connector) containers** — each capable of 100+ concurrent pipeline executions

**Active-active multi-node configuration for HA** — node failure causes automatic redistribution

**Stateless by design** — pipeline definitions and configuration are stored in the Manager, not on the node. New nodes are operational within minutes of deployment

**All connector credentials encrypted and stored locally** within the Ground Plex; never transmitted to SnapLogic cloud

**Fully streaming execution architecture** — Snaps process data as a stream rather than loading full datasets into memory, enabling high-throughput with predictable resource usage

[BOX:info]
**IMAGE: GROUND PLEX ARCHITECTURE DIAGRAM**

Insert: SnapLogic official Ground Plex on OpenShift architecture diagram showing JCC containers, Ground Plex node structure, and outbound HTTPS to Manager. Source from SnapLogic product/marketing team or use the SVG diagram above.
[/BOX]

**DEPLOYMENT SPECIFICATIONS**

**Container runtime**: Docker on RedHat OpenShift (Kubernetes)

**Resource requirements per node**:
- CPU: 8 cores minimum, 16 cores recommended for production
- Memory: 32GB minimum, 64GB recommended
- Storage: 100GB for logs and temporary processing files

**Scalability**: Horizontal scaling by adding Ground Plex nodes. Each node adds execution capacity. Typical production deployments: 2-4 nodes for redundancy and capacity.

**Network requirements**:
- Outbound HTTPS (port 443) to SnapLogic Manager (*.snaplogic.com)
- No inbound connections required
- Internal connectivity to {{customer_name}} data sources (SAP, Oracle, file systems, APIs)

**High Availability**: Active-active configuration across multiple nodes. Node failure triggers automatic redistribution of scheduled pipelines to remaining nodes. No single point of failure.

**Monitoring & Observability**:
- Real-time dashboard in SnapLogic Manager showing Ground Plex health, pipeline execution status, error rates
- Integration with Prometheus/Grafana for custom monitoring dashboards
- SNMP trap support for integration with {{customer_name}} enterprise monitoring tools
- Syslog export for centralized logging

subsections.title: SnapLogic Manager — Control Plane
subsections.content:
The SnapLogic Manager is the cloud-hosted control plane providing the Designer UI, metadata repository, scheduling engine, and audit logging. For {{customer_name}}'s deployment, the Manager handles only metadata — never customer data.

**Key Manager Functions:**

**Pipeline Designer**: Web-based visual canvas for building integration pipelines using drag-and-drop Snaps (connectors and transformations)

**Metadata Repository**: Centralized storage for pipeline definitions, Snap configurations, project structure, and RBAC policies

**Scheduling & Orchestration**: Cron-based scheduling, triggered execution, and API-initiated pipeline runs. Schedules are stored in Manager; execution happens in Ground Plex

**User Authentication & RBAC**: SSO integration (SAML 2.0), MFA support, role-based access control for Orgs, Projects, and pipelines

**Audit Logging**: Immutable audit trail of user actions, pipeline executions, data lineage, and system events

**Dashboard & Analytics**: Real-time visibility into pipeline execution status, error rates, data volumes, and Ground Plex health

**SnapGPT AI Assistant**: Natural language pipeline generation, intelligent Snap recommendations, and pipeline optimization suggestions

**Manager-to-Ground-Plex Communication:**

- Ground Plex initiates outbound HTTPS connection to Manager
- Manager sends pipeline definitions, schedules, and configuration
- Ground Plex sends execution status, logs, and metrics back to Manager
- No customer data transmitted in either direction

**Data Sovereignty for {{customer_name}}:**

All customer data remains within {{customer_name}}'s infrastructure. The Manager sees only:
- Pipeline execution status (success, failure, warning)
- Execution duration and record counts (aggregate metrics, not actual data)
- Error messages and stack traces (no PII or sensitive data)
- User authentication events and RBAC configuration

The Manager never sees:
- Actual customer data being processed
- Database query results or API responses
- File contents or message payloads
- Connector credentials (stored encrypted in Ground Plex)

subsections.title: Security & Data Governance
subsections.content:
SnapLogic provides enterprise-grade security controls required for aerospace manufacturing deployments:

**ENCRYPTION**

- **At rest**: AES-256 encryption for all stored data (pipeline definitions, credentials, logs)
- **In transit**: TLS 1.3 for all network communications (Manager ↔ Ground Plex, Ground Plex ↔ data sources)
- **Credential storage**: All connector credentials encrypted using AES-256 and stored locally in Ground Plex (never transmitted to SnapLogic cloud)

**AUTHENTICATION & ACCESS CONTROL**

- **SSO integration**: SAML 2.0 support for integration with {{customer_name}} identity provider (Active Directory, Okta, Azure AD)
- **Multi-factor authentication (MFA)**: Mandatory MFA enforcement for privileged accounts
- **Role-based access control (RBAC)**: Granular permissions at Org, Project Space, Project, and pipeline levels
- **API token authentication**: Secure API access for automated pipeline execution and integration with CI/CD tools

**AUDIT & COMPLIANCE**

- **Immutable audit logs**: Full trail of user actions, pipeline executions, and system events
- **Data lineage tracking**: End-to-end visibility of data flow from source to destination
- **Execution logs**: Detailed logs of every pipeline execution with success/failure status, error messages, and record counts
- **Compliance reporting**: Export audit logs and execution history for regulatory compliance review

**NETWORK SECURITY**

- **Outbound-only communication**: Ground Plex initiates all connections to Manager (no inbound firewall rules required)
- **IP whitelisting**: Restrict Ground Plex communication to SnapLogic Manager IP ranges
- **VPN/Private Link support**: Option to route Manager ↔ Ground Plex traffic over VPN or AWS PrivateLink for additional network isolation

**DATA GOVERNANCE**

- **Data masking**: Built-in Snaps for PII masking, tokenization, and anonymization
- **Data quality validation**: Schema validation, data type checking, null/duplicate detection
- **Error handling**: Configurable error routing, retry policies, and alerting for data quality issues
- **Metadata tagging**: Tag pipelines and data assets with business glossary terms, data classification, and ownership information

subsections.title: Monitoring & Management
subsections.content:
SnapLogic provides comprehensive monitoring and operational management capabilities:

[IMAGE:assets/images/customer/airbus_vendor_profile/Screenshot 2026-04-27 at 21.20.06.png:Monitoring and Management Dashboard]

**Real-Time Dashboard**: Web-based dashboard showing Ground Plex health, active pipeline executions, error rates, and resource utilization

**Alerting**: Configurable alerts for pipeline failures, Ground Plex node failures, and performance degradation. Alerts via email, Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook

**Metrics Export**: Integration with Prometheus/Grafana for custom dashboards and long-term metric storage

**SNMP Trap Support**: Integration with enterprise monitoring tools (HP OpenView, IBM Tivoli, BMC Patrol)

**Syslog Export**: Centralized logging export to {{customer_name}} log aggregation platforms

**Performance Monitoring**:
- Pipeline execution duration trends
- Data throughput (records/second, MB/second)
- Resource utilization (CPU, memory, disk I/O per Ground Plex node)
- Connector response times (identify slow database queries or API calls)

**Capacity Planning**:
- Historical execution metrics for trend analysis
- Predictive alerts when approaching capacity limits
- Recommendations for Ground Plex node scaling

**Operational Dashboards**:
- Executive view: High-level pipeline success rates, data volumes processed
- Operations view: Active executions, error queue, scheduled pipeline status
- Developer view: Individual pipeline execution logs, Snap-level debugging
